contribution.position: I hold my earlier position, and the QA seat's claim sharpens it. QA says peak_cpu is 55%, inside the 70% budget, citing artifact:perf-report. That artifact says peak_cpu measured 93% at peak load against a 70% budget. QA's figure is not in the artifact list, so I can't accept it. At 93% the budget is exceeded by 23 points, not met with room to spare. The risk conclusion built on 55% therefore has no support in the cited evidence. If a separate run measured 55%, it needs to be added as an artifact with its load profile and the reason it differs from the 93% run. Ops (artifact:ops-runbook) shows deploy and rollback steps exist, which helps recovery. It says nothing about preventing or capping retry storms, and artifact:incident-log shows two sev2 incidents from exactly that cause last quarter. Rollback after a storm has started is not the same as showing the storm cannot start. Product's cost margin (artifact:cost-sheet, 3% against a 5% ceiling) is a separate axis and doesn't offset this. The missing evidence is unchanged: a peak-load test showing retries and backoff stay bounded, a reconciled CPU number (or an explicit acceptance of the overage), and confirmation that last quarter's retry-storm root causes are fixed or capped. artifact:test-report (412 passed, 87% coverage) covers functional correctness and does not substitute for any of these.
